Counsel for Applicant :- Rishi Raj Kumar Yadav,Jitendra Kumar,Neeraj Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Neeraj Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.

2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 19 of 2022, under Sections 420 IPC and Section 66(c) of I.T. Act, Police Station Cyber Crime, District Prayagraj, with a prayer to enlarge her on anticipatory bail.
3.

entities.text: Police Station Cyber Crime, District Prayagraj
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, four accused persons, Ritik Kumar, Devendra Kumar Chelak, Yogendra Kumar Bharti and Dipti Singh are stated to have been arrested by police involved in making phone calls to several persons thereby duping them of their hard earned money on the pretext that they shall be married.

The applicant and other co-accused persons are stated to be the employees who Simmi vs State Of U.P.And Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169587089/
1 used to make calls.
4.

entities.text: Simmi vs State Of U.P.And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has apprehension of her arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
Learned counsel has further stated that she is not arrested from the spot.
Her name has come up in the statement of arrested co-accused person, although, she is named in the FIR.
The said statement of arrested co-accused person is not admissible in evidence.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against her.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal history.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, she will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

6. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that she has no criminal history.

7. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

sentences.text: 8. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may be adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
